newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin says France must tackle public deficit.
newsitem.headline: Jospin says France must tackle public deficit.

text.p: French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, reaffirming his commitment to a single European currency, pledged on Thursday that the government would tackle the country's public deficit.
"We have the goal of monetary union and we want to do it because we believe it is necessary," he told France 2 television. But "we must fight against deficits even if there were not monetary union."
He promised that if the new Socialist-led government had to make an effort to prevent "an excessive overshoot (in the public deficit), the burden will be shared equally".

He said no decisions had yet been taken and his comment that the impact of any measures would be shared out equally appeared meant to dampen speculation that the deficit will be curbed through higher corporate taxes.

Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said earlier on Thursday that the public deficit could be significantly higher than the 3.0 percent of gross domestic product forecast by the previous centre-right government.

Jospin declined to comment on what level of deficit he would consider acceptable for entry to a single currency in 1999, but said any measures to reduce the deficit must not hinder growth. "We must curb public spending without stifling growth," he said.
